243	**1.39** "**Total Estimated Remediation Costs**" means Twenty-Eight Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,400,000), as set forth in Section 5.1 and Exhibit C of this Agreement, representing the estimated total cost of Remedial Action at the Site based upon the preferred remedial alternative identified in the RI/FS.
244	
245	**1.40** "**Undisclosed Pre-Acquisition Conditions**" has the meaning set forth in Section 8.3 of this Agreement.
246	
247	## ARTICLE II --- JURISDICTION AND VENUE
248	
249	**Section 2.1** *Jurisdiction.* The Thurston County Superior Court has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Chapter 70A.305 RCW, including the authority to enter consent decrees in actions brought by Ecology under MTCA for the remediation of contaminated sites within the State of Washington. This Agreement is entered into pursuant to the Court's jurisdiction under MTCA and the general jurisdiction of the superior courts of the State of Washington.
250	
251	**Section 2.2** *Entry as Consent Decree.* This Agreement shall be submitted to the Thurston County Superior Court for entry as a Consent Decree in the matter captioned State of Washington, Department of Ecology v. Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc., Puget Metalworks, LLC, and Northshore Chemical Supply Co., Case No. 25-2-01847-34. Upon entry by the Court, this Agreement shall be enforceable as a court order, and any Party may seek judicial enforcement of its terms through proceedings before the Court. The Parties consent to the entry of this Agreement as a Consent Decree without further notice or hearing, except as may be required by applicable law or court rule.
252	
253	**Section 2.3** *Venue.* Venue is proper in Thurston County, Washington, as the county in which Ecology's headquarters are located and in accordance with RCW 70A.305 and applicable Washington venue statutes. The Parties agree that Thurston County is a convenient and appropriate forum for the resolution of disputes arising under this Agreement.
254	
255	**Section 2.4** *Consent to Jurisdiction.* Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction of the Thurston County Superior Court for purposes of the enforcement of this Agreement and waives any objection to venue in Thurston County, including any objection based on inconvenient forum, improper venue, or lack of personal jurisdiction. Nothing in this Section 2.4 shall be construed to limit any Party's right to remove an action to federal court where federal jurisdiction exists.
256	
257	## ARTICLE III --- PARTIES AND AUTHORITY
258	
259	**Section 3.1** *Identification of Parties.*
260	
261	(a) **Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc.** is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal place of business at 1100 SW Sixth Avenue, Suite 2400, Portland, Oregon 97204. Cascadia is the current owner of the Site, the sole member of Puget Metalworks, LLC, and the Lead Settling Party under this Agreement.
262	
263	(b) **Northshore Chemical Supply Co.** is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Washington, with its principal place of business at 3825 Evergreen Way, Everett, Washington 98201. Northshore is the Contributing Settling Party under this Agreement. Northshore is a privately held company, the equity interests of which are held by the Kowalski family trust.
264	
265	(c) **Puget Metalworks, LLC** is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Puget Metalworks is a wholly owned subsidiary of Cascadia and is the Operating Settling Party under this Agreement. Puget Metalworks is currently dormant and ceased all operations in 2016.
266	
267	(d) **Washington State Department of Ecology** is an agency of the State of Washington, with its headquarters located in Olympia, Washington. Ecology is the state agency responsible for administering and enforcing MTCA and is the Plaintiff/Petitioner in this action.
268	
269	**Section 3.2** *Authority to Execute.* Each person signing this Agreement on behalf of a Party represents and warrants that such person has been duly authorized to execute and deliver this Agreement on behalf of such Party and that this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Margaret Chen-Woodward, General Counsel of Cascadia, is authorized to execute this Agreement on behalf of Cascadia; Derek Kowalski, Chief Executive Officer of Northshore, is authorized to execute this Agreement on behalf of Northshore; and Raymond Ostrander, as the sole remaining manager of Puget Metalworks, is authorized to execute this Agreement on behalf of Puget Metalworks.
270	
271	**Section 3.3** *Legal Counsel.* Cascadia is represented in this matter by the law firm of Hargrove & Tillman LLP, 900 SW Fifth Avenue, Suite 1800, Portland, Oregon 97204, Attention: Victoria Sandoval. Northshore is represented in this matter by the law firm of Kellner Marsh & Associates LLP, 1201 Third Avenue, Suite 3400, Seattle, Washington 98101. Puget Metalworks is represented by counsel to Cascadia. Ecology is represented by the Washington State Attorney General's Office.
272	
273	**Section 3.4** *Status of Puget Metalworks.* The Parties acknowledge that Puget Metalworks, LLC is a dormant entity that ceased all business operations in 2016 and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Cascadia. Puget Metalworks has no material independent assets, no ongoing operations, no employees, and no revenue. Notwithstanding its dormant status, Puget Metalworks remains a separate legal entity organized under the laws of the State of Washington and is treated as a separate Settling Party for purposes of this Agreement. Raymond Ostrander, as the sole remaining manager of Puget Metalworks, has been authorized by Cascadia, as the sole member, to execute this Agreement on behalf of Puget Metalworks.
274	
275	## ARTICLE IV --- FINDINGS OF FACT AND REGULATORY BACKGROUND
276	
277	**Section 4.1** *Site History.* The Site, located at 2740 Tideflats Way, Tacoma, Washington 98421, was developed as an industrial electroplating facility and operated continuously from approximately 1972 through 2016. During the period of active operations, the facility conducted chromium electroplating (including hard chrome and decorative chrome processes utilizing hexavalent chromium solutions), cadmium plating, nickel plating, and solvent degreasing utilizing trichloroethylene ("TCE") and other chlorinated solvents. The facility processed metal components for aerospace, automotive, and marine industry clients. Operations generated significant quantities of hazardous waste and hazardous substances, including spent plating bath solutions containing hexavalent chromium, cadmium, nickel, and various acid compounds; wastewater treatment sludges containing heavy metals; and waste TCE and other chlorinated solvents. The facility ceased operations in 2016 following Cascadia's acquisition of Puget Metalworks.
278	
279	**Section 4.2** *Contamination.* The 2019 Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and the subsequent RI/FS identified extensive contamination of soil and groundwater at and in the vicinity of the Site. The primary contaminants of concern and their maximum detected concentrations are as follows:
280	
281	(a) *Trichloroethylene (TCE) in Groundwater.* TCE was detected in groundwater beneath and downgradient of the Site at concentrations up to 4,800 µg/L. The applicable MTCA cleanup level for TCE in groundwater under WAC 173-340-720 is 5 µg/L. The TCE groundwater plume extends approximately 1,200 feet beyond the northern boundary of the Site in the direction of Commencement Bay.
282	
283	(b) *Hexavalent Chromium in Soil.* Hexavalent chromium was detected in surface and subsurface soil at the Site at concentrations up to 12,300 mg/kg. The applicable MTCA cleanup level for hexavalent chromium in soil under WAC 173-340-740 is 19 mg/kg.
284	
285	(c) *Cadmium in Soil.* Cadmium was detected in surface and subsurface soil at the Site at concentrations up to 890 mg/kg. The applicable MTCA cleanup level for cadmium in soil under WAC 173-340-740 is 2 mg/kg.
286	
287	The contamination extends both laterally and vertically, with the deepest contamination detected at approximately sixty-five (65) feet below ground surface. The off-site groundwater plume poses potential risks to ecological receptors in Commencement Bay, including marine organisms and associated food webs.
288	
289	**Section 4.3** *Regulatory History.* On March 15, 2021, Ecology issued Agreed Order No. DE-2021-04892 pursuant to RCW 70A.305.040, naming Cascadia and Puget Metalworks as PLPs and requiring the investigation of contamination at the Site and the performance of interim remedial actions. On September 8, 2022, Ecology issued an Amended Agreed Order adding Northshore as a PLP based upon evidence that Northshore arranged for the supply, delivery, and use of TCE, hexavalent chromium compounds, and other hazardous substances at the Site during the period from 1978 through 2003.
290	
291	**Section 4.4** *Statutory Framework.* The investigation and remediation of the Site is governed by the Washington Model Toxics Control Act, Chapter 70A.305 RCW, and the implementing regulations at Chapter 173-340 WAC. MTCA establishes a comprehensive framework for the identification, investigation, and cleanup of sites contaminated by hazardous substances. Liability under MTCA is strict, joint, and several, and does not require a showing of fault or a causal nexus to specific contamination activities. RCW 70A.305.040 provides that any person who is an owner or operator of a facility, or who arranged for the disposal or treatment of hazardous substances at a facility, or who accepted hazardous substances for transport to a facility, is a Potentially Liable Person and is strictly liable for all remedial action costs. The Parties acknowledge that the allocation of costs and indemnification obligations set forth in this Agreement is a contractual allocation among the Settling Parties and does not alter or limit the statutory liability of any PLP under MTCA.
292	
293	**Section 4.5** *Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study.* The RI/FS was prepared by Clearwater Environmental Consulting, LLC, and was completed in October 2024. The RI/FS characterizes the nature and extent of contamination at the Site, evaluates potential remedial alternatives, and identifies a preferred remedial alternative consisting of source area excavation and off-site disposal, installation and operation of a groundwater extraction and treatment system, long-term monitoring, and implementation of institutional and engineering controls. The RI/FS provides the technical basis for the Remediation Work Plan attached as Exhibit B and for the cost estimates set forth in Article V.
294	
295	## ARTICLE V --- COST ALLOCATION AND PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS
296	
297	**Section 5.1** *Total Estimated Remediation Costs.* Based upon the RI/FS and the Remediation Work Plan (Exhibit B), the Parties have agreed that the Total Estimated Remediation Costs for the Site are Twenty-Eight Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,400,000), which costs comprise the following categories:
298	
299	(a) Source area excavation and off-site disposal: \$8,200,000;
300	
301	(b) Groundwater extraction and treatment system (design, construction, and operation): \$11,600,000;
302	
303	(c) Long-term monitoring (thirty (30) years): \$4,800,000;
304	
305	(d) Institutional controls and engineering controls (including deed restrictions, cap maintenance, and vapor mitigation): \$1,900,000; and
306	
307	(e) Contingency (approximately 7.04% of the sum of categories (a) through (d)): \$1,900,000.
308	
309	The foregoing categories sum to \$28,400,000, which constitutes the Total Estimated Remediation Costs for purposes of this Agreement.
310	
311	**Section 5.2** *Cost Shares.* The Total Estimated Remediation Costs shall be allocated among the Settling Parties as follows:
312	
313	(a) *Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc.* (as successor to Puget Metalworks and current owner of the Site): Sixty-Two Percent (62%), equal to Seventeen Million Six Hundred Eight Thousand Dollars (\$17,608,000);
314	
315	(b) *Northshore Chemical Supply Co.* (as arranger/transporter of hazardous substances): Twenty-Eight Percent (28%), equal to Seven Million Nine Hundred Fifty-Two Thousand Dollars (\$7,952,000); and
316	
317	(c) *Puget Metalworks, LLC* (as former operator): Ten Percent (10%), equal to Two Million Eight Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$2,840,000).
318	
319	The foregoing allocations reflect the Parties' negotiated apportionment of responsibility based upon each Settling Party's respective role in the contamination of the Site and are not a judicial determination of comparative fault.
320	
321	**Section 5.3** *Cascadia Guarantee of Puget Metalworks' Share.* Cascadia unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees the payment and performance of all of Puget Metalworks' Cost Share obligations under this Agreement, including the payment of Puget Metalworks' ten percent (10%) Cost Share of \$2,840,000 and any additional cost obligations that may arise under Section 5.6. In the event Puget Metalworks fails to satisfy any payment or performance obligation under this Agreement, Cascadia shall be directly and immediately liable for such obligation as if it were Cascadia's own obligation, without regard to any requirement that Ecology or any other Party first exhaust remedies against Puget Metalworks. This guarantee is a guarantee of payment and performance and not merely a guarantee of collection.
322	
323	**Section 5.4** *Escrow Deposit.* Northshore shall deposit its full Cost Share of Seven Million Nine Hundred Fifty-Two Thousand Dollars (\$7,952,000) into escrow with Ridgeway Escrow Services, Inc. (the "Escrow Agent") within five (5) business days of the execution of this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge that Northshore made such deposit on January 15, 2025. All escrowed funds shall be held in an interest-bearing account at First Columbia Bank, N.A., Tacoma branch. Interest earned on escrowed funds shall accrue for the benefit of Northshore. Disbursements from the escrow account shall be made in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement, upon joint authorization by Cascadia and Northshore or upon order of the Court.
324	
325	**Section 5.5** *Escrow Fees.* The annual escrow administration fee of Eighteen Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$18,500) charged by Ridgeway Escrow Services, Inc. shall be split equally between Cascadia (Nine Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$9,250)) and Northshore (Nine Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$9,250)), payable annually in advance on the anniversary of the Effective Date.
326	
327	**Section 5.6** *Cost Adjustments.* If actual remediation costs exceed the Total Estimated Remediation Costs of \$28,400,000, each Settling Party's additional obligation shall be determined in accordance with the same Cost Share percentages set forth in Section 5.2 (Cascadia: 62%; Northshore: 28%; Puget Metalworks: 10%), unless otherwise agreed in writing by all Settling Parties or ordered by the Court. The contingency amount set forth in Section 5.1(e) shall be applied first to cover any cost overruns before any additional assessments are levied against the Settling Parties. If actual remediation costs are less than the Total Estimated Remediation Costs, any surplus funds shall be returned to the Settling Parties in proportion to their respective Cost Shares.
328	
329	**Section 5.7** *Cost Share Table.* The following table summarizes the cost allocation among the Settling Parties:
330	
331	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
332	  Settling Party                       Role                          Percentage      Dollar Amount
333	  ------------------------------------ ----------------------------- --------------- ------------------
334	  Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc.   Lead Settling Party           62%             \$17,608,000
335	
336	  Northshore Chemical Supply Co.       Contributing Settling Party   28%             \$7,952,000
337	
338	  Puget Metalworks, LLC                Operating Settling Party      10%             \$2,840,000
339	
340	  **Total**                                                          **100%**        **\$28,400,000**
341	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
342	
343	## ARTICLE VI --- REMEDIATION OBLIGATIONS
344	
345	**Section 6.1** *Lead Settling Party Responsibilities.* Cascadia, as Lead Settling Party, shall manage and oversee all Remedial Actions at the Site, including the retention and direction of Clearwater Environmental Consulting, LLC, and any other contractors, subcontractors, or consultants necessary to perform the Remedial Action. Cascadia shall be responsible for the day-to-day management of all remediation activities, including but not limited to procurement, scheduling, contractor oversight, health and safety compliance, and community relations. Cascadia shall act in good faith and in a manner consistent with the Remediation Work Plan and the requirements of MTCA in discharging its responsibilities under this Section 6.1.
346	
347	**Section 6.2** *Remediation Work Plan.* All Remedial Actions at the Site shall be conducted in accordance with the Remediation Work Plan attached hereto as Exhibit B, as approved by Ecology and as may be amended from time to time with Ecology's prior written approval. The Remediation Work Plan sets forth the scope, sequencing, methodology, and schedule for all remediation activities, including source area excavation, groundwater extraction and treatment system design, construction, and operation, long-term monitoring, and the implementation of institutional and engineering controls. All work performed under the Remediation Work Plan shall conform to applicable MTCA cleanup standards and WAC 173-340 requirements.
348	
349	**Section 6.3** *Compliance with MTCA.* All Remedial Actions performed at the Site shall comply with the applicable MTCA cleanup standards set forth in WAC 173-340, including without limitation the Cleanup Standards defined in Section 1.4 of this Agreement. The Settling Parties shall not seek or agree to any cleanup standard less stringent than those set forth in WAC 173-340 without Ecology's prior written approval. All remediation activities shall be conducted in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and permits.
350	
351	**Section 6.4** *Access and Cooperation.* Each Settling Party shall cooperate fully with the Remedial Actions and shall provide reasonable access to information, documents, records, and personnel relevant to the investigation and remediation of the Site. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Northshore shall provide all reasonably available records relating to its historical supply of hazardous substances to the Site, including invoices, shipping records, material safety data sheets, product specifications, and correspondence with Puget Metalworks relating to the delivery and use of TCE, hexavalent chromium compounds, cadmium compounds, and other hazardous substances. Cascadia shall provide access to the Site to Ecology, its contractors, and the other Settling Parties as reasonably necessary for the performance of the Remedial Action.
352	
353	**Section 6.5** *Reporting.* Cascadia shall provide quarterly progress reports to Ecology and to each of the other Settling Parties regarding the status of the Remedial Action, including a summary of work completed during the reporting period, work planned for the next reporting period, any deviations from the Remediation Work Plan, expenditures to date, and any significant findings or developments. Quarterly reports shall be submitted no later than the fifteenth (15th) day following the end of each calendar quarter. In addition, Cascadia shall promptly notify Ecology and the other Settling Parties of any emergency, spill, release, or other event that may affect the progress or scope of the Remedial Action.
354	
355	**Section 6.6** *Financial Assurance.* Cascadia has provided, and shall maintain in effect throughout the duration of the Remedial Action, Financial Assurance Bond No. FA-2025-3317, issued by Hollcroft Point Surety Group in the amount of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000), effective February 1, 2025, in the form attached as Exhibit E, to secure the performance of Cascadia's Remedial Action obligations under this Agreement. In the event the Financial Assurance Bond is drawn upon, cancelled, or reduced below Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000), Cascadia shall, within thirty (30) days, obtain a replacement financial assurance instrument acceptable to Ecology in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000).
356	
357	## ARTICLE VII --- COVENANT NOT TO SUE AND RESERVATION OF RIGHTS
358	
359	**Section 7.1** *Ecology's Covenant Not to Sue.* Subject to the reservations set forth in Section 7.3, Ecology covenants not to sue or take administrative or judicial action against the Settling Parties or any of them for any claims, causes of action, or demands arising from or relating to the contamination at the Site that are addressed by this Consent Decree, provided that the Settling Parties comply with their respective obligations under this Agreement. This covenant not to sue is conditioned upon the satisfactory performance by each Settling Party of its obligations hereunder, including the timely payment of all Cost Share amounts, the diligent performance of Remedial Actions, and compliance with all reporting and cooperation requirements. This covenant extends to the officers, directors, employees, and agents of each Settling Party to the extent such persons are acting within the scope of their duties for such Settling Party.
360	
361	**Section 7.2** *Settling Parties' Covenant Not to Sue.* Each Settling Party covenants not to assert any claim, cause of action, or demand against any other Settling Party for matters addressed in this Consent Decree, except as expressly provided in Article VIII (Indemnification) and Article XI (Dispute Resolution) of this Agreement. This covenant not to sue does not extend to claims arising from a material breach of this Agreement by another Settling Party, which claims shall be subject to the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article XI.
362	
363	**Section 7.3** *Ecology's Reserved Rights.* Ecology reserves the right to take further administrative, judicial, or regulatory action against any or all of the Settling Parties, notwithstanding the covenant not to sue set forth in Section 7.1, under the following circumstances:
364	
365	(a) Conditions at the Site pose an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health or the environment that is not adequately addressed by the Remedial Actions required under this Agreement;
366	
367	(b) Information not known to Ecology at the time of the entry of this Consent Decree reveals previously unknown conditions at or relating to the Site that require additional remedial action beyond the scope of this Agreement;
368	
369	(c) Any Settling Party fails to comply with a material obligation under this Agreement and does not cure such failure within sixty (60) days after written notice from Ecology; or
370	
371	(d) Natural Resource Damage claims are asserted by a tribal trustee, federal trustee, or other natural resource trustee, and Ecology's covenant not to sue shall not be construed as a release or waiver of NRD claims on behalf of any such trustee.
372	
373	**Section 7.4** *Contribution Protection.* Pursuant to RCW 70A.305.040(4)(b), each Settling Party that has resolved its liability to the State under this Consent Decree shall receive contribution protection to the extent of its Cost Share for matters addressed in this Agreement. No Settling Party shall be liable for claims for contribution regarding matters addressed in this Consent Decree, except as among the Settling Parties as provided in Article VIII and Article XI of this Agreement.
374	
375	## ARTICLE VIII --- INDEMNIFICATION
376	
377	**Section 8.1** *Cascadia's Indemnification of Northshore.*
378	
379	(a) Cascadia shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Northshore and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives (collectively, the "Northshore Indemnified Parties") from and against any and all Losses arising from Cascadia's or Puget Metalworks' Remedial Actions at or relating to the Site, including without limitation any Third-Party Claims arising from the conduct, management, oversight, or performance of Remedial Actions by Cascadia, Puget Metalworks, or any contractor, subcontractor, or agent retained by Cascadia or Puget Metalworks in connection with the Remedial Action. For the avoidance of doubt, this indemnification covers Losses arising from Cascadia's or Puget Metalworks' remediation activities, including claims for personal injury, property damage, or economic loss asserted by third parties as a result of such activities.
380	
381	(b) *Cap.* Cascadia's aggregate indemnification obligation to the Northshore Indemnified Parties under this Section 8.1 shall not exceed Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000), regardless of the number of claims or the aggregate Losses asserted.
382	
383	(c) *Deductible.* Cascadia shall have no obligation to indemnify the Northshore Indemnified Parties under this Section 8.1 unless and until the aggregate amount of Losses for which indemnification is sought under this Section 8.1 exceeds Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) (the "Section 8.1 Deductible"), and thereafter Cascadia shall be liable only for the amount of such Losses in excess of the Section 8.1 Deductible. For clarification, the Northshore Indemnified Parties shall bear and shall not be entitled to recover the first Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) of aggregate Losses under this Section 8.1.
384	
385	**Section 8.2** *Northshore's Indemnification of Cascadia.*
386	
387	(a) Northshore shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Cascadia and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives (collectively, the "Cascadia Indemnified Parties") from and against any and all Losses arising from Northshore's historical supply of Hazardous Substances to the Site during the period from 1978 to 2003, including without limitation any Third-Party Claims arising from the arrangement for disposal or treatment of Hazardous Substances at the Site by Northshore, the delivery, transportation, or sale of TCE, hexavalent chromium compounds, cadmium compounds, or other Hazardous Substances to the Site by Northshore, or the release or threatened release of Hazardous Substances at or from the Site attributable to substances supplied by Northshore.
388	
389	(b) *Cap.* Northshore's aggregate indemnification obligation to the Cascadia Indemnified Parties under this Section 8.2 shall not exceed Seven Million Nine Hundred Fifty-Two Thousand Dollars (\$7,952,000), an amount equal to Northshore's Cost Share as set forth in Section 5.2(b).
390	
391	(c) *Threshold.* Northshore shall have no obligation to indemnify the Cascadia Indemnified Parties under this Section 8.2 unless and until the aggregate amount of Losses for which indemnification is sought under this Section 8.2 equals or exceeds One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000) (the "Section 8.2 Threshold"), and upon such aggregate Losses equaling or exceeding the Section 8.2 Threshold, Northshore shall be liable for the full amount of such Losses from the first dollar thereof, subject to the aggregate cap set forth in Section 8.2(b). For clarification, the Section 8.2 Threshold operates as a triggering mechanism: once the aggregate amount of qualifying Losses meets or exceeds One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000), Northshore's indemnification obligation covers the entire amount of such Losses, including amounts below the Section 8.2 Threshold, up to the aggregate cap.
392	
393	**Section 8.3** *Puget Metalworks' Indemnification.*
394	
395	(a) Puget Metalworks shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each of Cascadia and Northshore and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from and against any and all Losses arising from environmental conditions at the Site that (i) existed prior to Cascadia's acquisition of Puget Metalworks in 2016, and (ii) were not disclosed to Cascadia in connection with such acquisition (collectively, "Undisclosed Pre-Acquisition Conditions"). This indemnification extends to Losses arising from Third-Party Claims, Government Cost Recovery Claims, and regulatory enforcement actions to the extent attributable to Undisclosed Pre-Acquisition Conditions.
396	
397	(b) *No Cap.* There shall be no aggregate cap on Puget Metalworks' indemnification obligations under this Section 8.3.
398	
399	(c) *No Basket.* There shall be no deductible, threshold, or minimum amount of Losses required before Puget Metalworks' indemnification obligations under this Section 8.3 become effective.
400	
401	(d) *Cascadia Guarantee.* Cascadia unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees the payment and performance of all of Puget Metalworks' indemnification obligations under this Section 8.3. In the event Puget Metalworks fails to satisfy any indemnification obligation under this Section 8.3, Cascadia shall be directly and immediately liable for such obligation as if it were Cascadia's own obligation, without regard to any requirement that the Indemnified Party first exhaust remedies against Puget Metalworks.
402	
403	**Section 8.4** *Government Cost Recovery Indemnification.*
404	
405	(a) In the event that Ecology, the United States Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA"), or any other federal, state, or local governmental entity asserts a claim for cost recovery, response costs, or remediation costs against any Settling Party that exceeds the scope of the matters addressed in this Consent Decree (a "Government Cost Recovery Claim"), each Settling Party shall indemnify the other Settling Parties for such Government Cost Recovery Claim in proportion to their respective Cost Shares as set forth in Section 5.2 (Cascadia: 62%; Northshore: 28%; Puget Metalworks: 10%).
406	
407	(b) *No Cap.* There shall be no aggregate cap on indemnification obligations under this Section 8.4.
408	
409	(c) *No Basket.* There shall be no deductible, threshold, or minimum amount required before indemnification obligations under this Section 8.4 become effective.
410	
411	(d) *Cross-Indemnification.* The indemnification obligations under this Section 8.4 are mutual: each Settling Party cross-indemnifies each other Settling Party in proportion to the indemnifying Settling Party's Cost Share percentage.
412	
413	**Section 8.5** *Natural Resource Damages Indemnification.*
414	
415	(a) In the event that any tribal trustee, federal trustee, or state trustee asserts a claim for Natural Resource Damages ("NRD") relating to the Site, including but not limited to claims arising from contamination of Commencement Bay, its shorelines, tidelands, submerged lands, or associated natural resources, the following allocation shall apply:
416	
417	<!-- -->
418	
419	(i) Northshore shall indemnify Cascadia for forty percent (40%) of any such NRD claim, including forty percent (40%) of all NRD assessment costs, damages, and associated litigation costs;
420	
421	(ii) Cascadia shall bear sixty percent (60%) of any such NRD claim; and
422	
423	(iii) Puget Metalworks shall have no indemnification obligation with respect to NRD claims under this Section 8.5.
424	
425	<!-- -->
426	
427	(b) *Cap on Northshore's NRD Indemnification.* Northshore's aggregate indemnification obligation for NRD claims under this Section 8.5 shall not exceed Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000). Once Northshore has paid or incurred NRD indemnification obligations totaling Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) under this Section 8.5, Northshore shall have no further NRD indemnification obligation, and Cascadia shall bear all NRD claims in excess of such amount.
428	
429	(c) *Rationale.* The Parties acknowledge that the NRD indemnification allocation set forth in this Section 8.5 differs from the general Cost Share percentages set forth in Section 5.2. This deviation reflects the Parties' assessment, based upon the RI/FS and the available technical evidence, that Northshore's supply of hexavalent chromium compounds to the Site was a disproportionate contributor to the contamination of Commencement Bay and its natural resources, and that the NRD exposure accordingly warrants a different allocation than the general remediation cost allocation. Puget Metalworks' exclusion from NRD indemnification reflects the Parties' determination that the remediation cost allocation in Section 5.2 adequately accounts for Puget Metalworks' share of NRD-related liability.
430	
431	**Section 8.6** *Excluded Claims.* The indemnification obligations set forth in Sections 8.1 and 8.2 of this Agreement shall not apply to:

440	
441	For the avoidance of doubt, the exclusions set forth in this Section 8.6 apply only to the indemnification obligations set forth in Sections 8.1 and 8.2, and do not apply to or limit the indemnification obligations set forth in Sections 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5.
442	
443	**Section 8.7** *Coordination with Insurance.*
444	
445	(a) The indemnification obligations of any Indemnifying Party under this Article VIII shall be reduced dollar-for-dollar by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received by the Indemnified Party (net of any applicable deductibles, self-insured retentions, and costs of recovery) with respect to the applicable Losses for which indemnification is sought.
446	
447	(b) Prior to seeking indemnification under this Article VIII, the Indemnified Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to pursue recovery under any applicable insurance policy, including the PLL Policy (Policy No. PLL-2023-08841, issued by Hollcroft Point Surety Group), and any other first-party or third-party insurance policies that may provide coverage for the applicable Losses. The Indemnified Party shall promptly notify the Indemnifying Party of any insurance claim submitted in respect of Losses for which indemnification may be sought, and shall keep the Indemnifying Party reasonably informed of the status of such insurance claim, including any coverage determination, reservation of rights, denial, or payment.
448	
449	(c) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Indemnified Party shall not be required to initiate or maintain litigation against its insurer as a condition to seeking indemnification under this Article VIII. The obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to pursue insurance shall not require the Indemnified Party to file suit, initiate arbitration, or engage in formal dispute resolution proceedings against its insurer.
450	
451	(d) The Indemnifying Party shall have no right to subrogate against, or seek contribution from, the Indemnified Party's insurer except to the extent expressly permitted by applicable law and the express terms of the relevant insurance policy. Nothing in this Section 8.7 shall be construed to create any rights in favor of any insurer or to alter the terms of any insurance policy.
452	
453	**Section 8.8** *Survival of Indemnification Obligations.*
454	
455	(a) The indemnification obligations set forth in Section 8.1 (Cascadia's Indemnification of Northshore) and Section 8.2 (Northshore's Indemnification of Cascadia) shall survive the Effective Date for a period of twelve (12) years, that is, through and including February 1, 2037, and shall terminate thereafter, except with respect to any claim for which a proper notice of claim has been delivered to the Indemnifying Party prior to such termination date in accordance with the procedures set forth in Exhibit D. Any claim for which proper notice has been delivered prior to the termination date shall survive until final resolution of such claim, notwithstanding the expiration of the twelve-year survival period.
456	
457	(b) The indemnification obligations set forth in Section 8.4 (Government Cost Recovery Indemnification) shall survive the Effective Date for a period of twenty (20) years, that is, through and including February 1, 2045.
458	
459	(c) The indemnification obligations set forth in Section 8.3 (Puget Metalworks' Indemnification for Undisclosed Pre-Acquisition Conditions) shall survive indefinitely and shall not be subject to any time limitation.
460	
461	(d) All survival periods set forth in this Section 8.8 are subject to any applicable statutes of limitation or repose under Washington law. Nothing in this Section 8.8 shall be construed to extend any otherwise applicable statute of limitation or statute of repose beyond its statutory term.
462	
463	**Section 8.9** *Assignment of Indemnification Rights.*
464	
465	(a) The indemnification rights and obligations under this Article VIII may not be assigned, transferred, or delegated by any Settling Party without the prior written consent of each Indemnifying Party affected by such assignment, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
466	
467	(b) Notwithstanding Section 8.9(a), a Settling Party may assign its indemnification rights (but not its indemnification obligations without the Indemnifying Party's consent) in connection with a sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of such Settling Party, provided that the assignee expressly assumes in writing all of the assigning Party's obligations under this Agreement and delivers to each other Settling Party a written instrument of assumption in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to each such Party.
468	
469	(c) Any purported assignment, transfer, or delegation in violation of this Section 8.9 shall be void and of no force or effect, and shall not relieve the assigning Party of any of its obligations under this Article VIII.
470	
471	## ARTICLE IX --- REMEDIATION WORK STANDARDS
472	
473	**Section 9.1** *General Standards.* All Remedial Actions at the Site shall be conducted in accordance with the applicable MTCA cleanup standards set forth in WAC 173-340 and in accordance with the Remediation Work Plan attached hereto as Exhibit B. The Settling Parties shall ensure that all work performed at the Site meets or exceeds the standards of care applicable to environmental remediation work in the State of Washington. All Remedial Actions shall be performed by qualified contractors and consultants with experience in the remediation of sites contaminated with chlorinated solvents and heavy metals.
474	
475	**Section 9.2** *Selection of Cleanup Standards.* The Cleanup Standards for the Site, as established pursuant to WAC 173-340 and as set forth in Section 1.4 of this Agreement, are as follows: (a) TCE at 5 µg/L in groundwater, based on the MTCA Method A cleanup level; (b) hexavalent chromium at 19 mg/kg in soil, based on the MTCA Method A cleanup level for unrestricted land use; and (c) cadmium at 2 mg/kg in soil, based on the MTCA Method A cleanup level for unrestricted land use. These Cleanup Standards shall apply to the Remedial Action unless modified by Ecology in writing based upon site-specific risk assessments or changed regulatory requirements.
476	
477	**Section 9.3** *Clearwater Oversight.* Clearwater Environmental Consulting, LLC shall serve as the joint environmental consultant for the Settling Parties and shall oversee all Remedial Actions at the Site. Clearwater's professional judgments regarding remediation methodology, sequencing, and technical approach shall be given deference by the Settling Parties, subject in all cases to Ecology's approval authority. Clearwater shall maintain appropriate professional liability insurance coverage throughout the duration of the Remedial Action. Any dispute regarding Clearwater's professional judgments shall be resolved in consultation with Ecology and, if necessary, through the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article XI.
478	
479	**Section 9.4** *Quality Assurance/Quality Control.* All sampling, analysis, testing, and remediation work performed at the Site shall comply with applicable quality assurance and quality control ("QA/QC") protocols, including without limitation the requirements of WAC 173-340-830 and any project-specific QA/QC plan approved by Ecology. All analytical work shall be performed by laboratories certified under the Washington State Department of Ecology laboratory accreditation program or equivalent accreditation. Chain-of-custody procedures, data validation protocols, and documentation requirements shall conform to applicable Ecology guidance.
480	
481	**Section 9.5** *Modifications to Remediation Work Plan.* Any material modification to the Remediation Work Plan (Exhibit B) shall require Ecology's prior written approval. The requesting party shall submit a written request for modification to Ecology and to all Settling Parties, describing the proposed modification, the rationale therefor, and any anticipated effect on the scope, schedule, or cost of the Remedial Action. Ecology shall respond to any request for modification within forty-five (45) days. Non-material modifications, including adjustments to sampling locations or scheduling, may be approved by Clearwater in consultation with Ecology without formal written amendment.
482	
483	## ARTICLE X --- FORCE MAJEURE
484	
485	**Section 10.1** *Definition of Force Majeure.* A "Force Majeure Event" means an event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of a Party that prevents or materially delays such Party's performance of its obligations under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) natural disasters, including earthquakes, floods, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, landslides, and severe weather events; (b) acts of war, terrorism, insurrection, or civil unrest; (c) government orders, embargoes, or sanctions (other than Ecology orders or directives relating to the Site); (d) epidemics, pandemics, or public health emergencies declared by a governmental authority; or (e) other events of similar magnitude that are not caused by and could not have been reasonably anticipated or prevented by the affected Party. Force Majeure Events do not include economic hardship, changes in market conditions, labor disputes that are within the Party's control, or the inability of a Party to obtain financing.
486	
487	**Section 10.2** *Notice and Mitigation.* A Party claiming a Force Majeure Event shall provide written notice to all other Parties within ten (10) business days of the occurrence of such event, describing the nature and expected duration of the Force Majeure Event and the obligations affected thereby. The Party claiming force majeure shall use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance as soon as practicable. The Party shall provide periodic updates to the other Parties regarding the status of the Force Majeure Event and its effect on performance.
488	
489	**Section 10.3** *Effect.* A Force Majeure Event shall not excuse any payment obligation under this Agreement but may extend performance deadlines (other than payment deadlines) for a period commensurate with the duration of the Force Majeure Event. If a Force Majeure Event continues for a period exceeding one hundred eighty (180) days, any Party may request that the Court modify the applicable performance deadlines or, if appropriate, the scope of the Remedial Action, subject to Ecology's approval. Nothing in this Article X shall limit Ecology's reserved rights under Section 7.3.
490	
491	## ARTICLE XI --- DISPUTE RESOLUTION
492	
493	**Section 11.1** *Informal Resolution.* In the event of any dispute, controversy, or disagreement arising under or relating to this Agreement (a "Dispute"), the Parties involved in such Dispute shall first attempt to resolve the matter through good-faith negotiation. The Party asserting the Dispute shall deliver written notice of the Dispute to the other Party or Parties involved, describing the nature of the Dispute and the relief sought. The Parties shall engage in good-faith negotiations for a period of thirty (30) days following delivery of such written notice. During the negotiation period, each Party shall designate a senior representative with authority to negotiate and resolve the Dispute. All communications during the negotiation period shall be confidential and inadmissible in any subsequent proceeding, except to the extent otherwise required by law.
494	
495	**Section 11.2** *Mediation.* If the Dispute is not resolved through informal negotiation within the thirty (30)-day period provided in Section 11.1, the Parties involved shall submit the Dispute to non-binding mediation before a mutually agreed-upon mediator. The mediation shall take place in Portland, Oregon or Seattle, Washington, as agreed by the Parties, or, if the Parties cannot agree, in Seattle, Washington. The costs of the mediator shall be shared equally among the Parties involved in the Dispute. Each Party shall bear its own attorneys' fees and costs in connection with the mediation. The mediator shall be a neutral person with expertise in environmental law, commercial disputes, or such other area of expertise as is relevant to the Dispute.
496	
497	**Section 11.3** *Arbitration or Litigation.* If mediation does not resolve the Dispute within sixty (60) days following the commencement of mediation, any Party involved in the Dispute may submit the matter to the Thurston County Superior Court for resolution in accordance with applicable law, including the enforcement provisions of this Consent Decree. Alternatively, if all Parties involved in the Dispute agree in writing, the Dispute may be submitted to binding arbitration in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association, with the arbitration to be conducted in Seattle, Washington. Nothing in this Section 11.3 shall limit any Party's right to seek emergency or injunctive relief from the Court at any time.
498	
499	**Section 11.4** *Ecology Disputes.* Disputes between the Settling Parties and Ecology regarding Ecology's exercise of its regulatory authority under MTCA, including disputes regarding the adequacy of the Remedial Action, the selection of cleanup standards, or the approval of modifications to the Remediation Work Plan, are not subject to this Article XI and shall be resolved under applicable administrative procedures established by MTCA and WAC 173-340, including the administrative appeals provisions of RCW 70A.305.070.
500	
501	**Section 11.5** *Indemnification Disputes.* Disputes arising under Article VIII (Indemnification) or the Indemnification Procedures set forth in Exhibit D shall be resolved in accordance with the procedures set forth in this Article XI. For the avoidance of doubt, any dispute regarding the obligation to indemnify, the amount of indemnifiable Losses, the applicability of any cap, basket, or exclusion, or the procedures for tendering and resolving indemnification claims shall be subject to the informal negotiation, mediation, and litigation/arbitration procedures of Sections 11.1 through 11.3.
502	
503	## ARTICLE XII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS
504	
505	**Section 12.1** *Entire Agreement.* This Agreement, together with the Exhibits attached hereto (Exhibits A through F), the Side Letter dated January 12, 2025, between Cascadia and Northshore, and the Escrow Agreement dated January 12, 2025, among Cascadia, Northshore, and Ridgeway Escrow Services, Inc., constitutes the entire agreement among the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, representations, warranties, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, among the Parties with respect to such subject matter. No Party has been induced to enter into this Agreement by any representation or warranty not expressly set forth in this Agreement.
506	
507	**Section 12.2** *Amendments.* No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by all Parties to this Agreement, and, to the extent required by the Court, approved and entered by the Court as an amendment to the Consent Decree. No oral agreements or understandings shall amend, modify, or supplement this Agreement.
508	
509	**Section 12.3** *Severability.* If any provision of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent practicable, achieves the economic, business, and legal objectives of the original provision.
510	
511	**Section 12.4** *Governing Law.* This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Washington, including the Washington Model Toxics Control Act, Chapter 70A.305 RCW, and the regulations promulgated thereunder, without regard to principles of conflicts of laws that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Delivery of an executed counterpart by facsimile or electronic transmission (including PDF) shall be as effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.

No waiver of any provision shall be construed as a waiver of any other provision or of such Party's right to enforce such provision in the future.

Upon entry by the Court, this Agreement shall have the full force and effect of a court order and shall be enforceable through contempt proceedings and other judicial remedies. # EXHIBIT D

## INDEMNIFICATION PROCEDURES

to the

**COMPREHENSIVE SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND CONSENT DECREE**

dated January 12, 2025

(the "Settlement Agreement")

Effective Date: February 1, 2025 Entered as a Consent Decree: February 14, 2025

Thurston County Superior Court Case No. 25-2-01847-34

This Exhibit D is attached to and incorporated by reference into the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement and Consent Decree dated January 12, 2025 (the "Settlement Agreement"), which was entered as a consent decree on February 14, 2025, in the Superior Court of the State of Washington for Thurston County, Case No. 25-2-01847-34, with an Effective Date of February 1, 2025. This Exhibit D governs the procedures for asserting, defending, and resolving indemnification claims arising under Article VIII (Sections 8.1 through 8.9) of the Settlement Agreement.

The parties to this Exhibit D are: **Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("Cascadia" or "Lead Settling Party"); **Northshore Chemical Supply Co.**, a Washington corporation ("Northshore" or "Contributing Settling Party"); and **Puget Metalworks, LLC**, a Washington limited liability company ("Puget Metalworks" or "Operating Settling Party"). Cascadia, Northshore, and Puget Metalworks are referred to collectively herein as the "Settling Parties" or the "Parties."

Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Exhibit D shall have the meanings ascribed to them in Article II of the Settlement Agreement.

## Section 1 --- Definitions

As used in this Exhibit D, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**"Business Day"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or day on which commercial banks in Portland, Oregon or Seattle, Washington are authorized or required by law or executive order to close.

**"Claim Notice"** means a written notice delivered by an Indemnified Party to an Indemnifying Party providing notice of a Third-Party Claim for which indemnification is sought under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, prepared and delivered in accordance with the requirements of Section 2 of this Exhibit D.

**"Defense Notice"** means a written notice delivered by an Indemnifying Party to an Indemnified Party electing to assume the defense of a Third-Party Claim in accordance with Section 3.1 of this Exhibit D.

**"Indemnified Party"** means the Party entitled to indemnification with respect to a particular claim under Sections 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5 of the Settlement Agreement, as applicable.

**"Indemnifying Party"** means the Party obligated to provide indemnification with respect to a particular claim under Sections 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5 of the Settlement Agreement, as applicable.

**"Third-Party Claim"** means any claim, demand, action, suit, proceeding, investigation, or notice asserted by any Person other than a Settling Party against an Indemnified Party for which indemnification may be sought under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, inter-party claims between or among Settling Parties are expressly excluded from the definition of Third-Party Claim and are not subject to the procedures set forth in this Exhibit D, as provided in Section 8.6(d) of the Settlement Agreement.

For reference, the Excluded Claims defined in Section 8.6 of the Settlement Agreement --- including claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence, claims related to contamination at sites other than 2740 Tideflats Way, Tacoma, WA 98421, claims for punitive, exemplary, or multiplied damages, and inter-party claims between or among Settling Parties --- are not eligible for indemnification under the procedures set forth in this Exhibit D or under Article VIII generally. Nothing in this Exhibit D shall be construed to expand or modify the scope of the Excluded Claims as defined in Section 8.6 of the Settlement Agreement.

## Section 2 --- Notice of Third-Party Claims

### 2.1 Obligation to Provide Claim Notice

Upon receipt by an Indemnified Party of any Third-Party Claim, whether by service of process, written demand, regulatory notice, administrative order, subpoena, or otherwise, the Indemnified Party shall deliver a Claim Notice to the Indemnifying Party (or, if more than one Party may have indemnification obligations with respect to such Third-Party Claim, to each such Indemnifying Party) within thirty (30) Business Days of the Indemnified Party's actual receipt of such Third-Party Claim.

Each Claim Notice shall be in writing and delivered in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 12.3 of the Settlement Agreement. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, notices shall be addressed as follows:

If to Cascadia: Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc., 1100 SW Sixth Avenue, Suite 2400, Portland, OR 97204, Attention: Margaret Chen-Woodward, General Counsel; with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to Hargrove & Tillman LLP, 900 SW Fifth Avenue, Suite 1800, Portland, OR 97204, Attention: Victoria Sandoval.

If to Northshore: Northshore Chemical Supply Co., 3825 Evergreen Way, Everett, WA 98201, Attention: Derek Kowalski, Chief Executive Officer; with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to Kellner Marsh & Associates LLP, Seattle, WA.

If to Puget Metalworks: Puget Metalworks, LLC, c/o Cascadia Industrial Holdings, Inc., 1100 SW Sixth Avenue, Suite 2400, Portland, OR 97204, Attention: Raymond Ostrander, Sole Remaining Manager.

### 2.2 Contents of Claim Notice

Each Claim Notice shall include the following:

(a) a description of the Third-Party Claim in reasonable detail, including the identity of the claimant and the nature and basis of the claim asserted;

(b) copies of all material documents relating to the Third-Party Claim that have been received by the Indemnified Party as of the date of the Claim Notice, including any complaint, petition, demand letter, subpoena, regulatory order, notice of violation, or similar document;

(c) a reference to the specific Section or Sections of Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement under which indemnification is sought (i.e., Section 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5, as applicable);

(d) a good-faith estimate of the potential liability or exposure arising from the Third-Party Claim, if reasonably determinable at the time the Claim Notice is delivered; and

(e) a statement of whether the Indemnified Party believes the Third-Party Claim is subject to any applicable cap, basket, or deductible under the relevant Section of Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, and, if so, an identification of the applicable limitation.

### 2.3 Effect of Late or Deficient Notice

The failure of an Indemnified Party to deliver a Claim Notice within the thirty (30) Business Day period specified in Section 2.1, or to include all of the information required by Section 2.2, shall not forfeit or waive the Indemnified Party's right to indemnification under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, unless the Indemnifying Party demonstrates that it was materially prejudiced by such delay or deficiency. The burden of proving material prejudice rests with the Indemnifying Party asserting that its indemnification obligation has been reduced or eliminated by reason of such delay or deficiency. Material prejudice includes, without limitation, the inability to participate meaningfully in early resolution or mediation of the Third-Party Claim, the loss of material evidence, the forfeiture of defenses that would have been available had timely notice been provided, or the expiration of applicable statutes of limitation on contribution or subrogation claims against third parties. A deficient Claim Notice may be supplemented by the Indemnified Party at any time, and such supplement shall cure any prior deficiency to the extent the information is provided before the Indemnifying Party has been materially prejudiced by the prior deficiency.

## Section 3 --- Defense of Third-Party Claims

### 3.1 Right to Assume Defense

The Indemnifying Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to assume the defense of any Third-Party Claim for which it may be obligated to provide indemnification under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement. To exercise this right, the Indemnifying Party must deliver a Defense Notice to the Indemnified Party within twenty (20) Business Days of the Indemnifying Party's receipt of the Claim Notice. The Defense Notice must include: (a) an acknowledgment that the Indemnifying Party accepts indemnification responsibility for the Third-Party Claim, subject to any applicable caps, baskets, deductibles, and exclusions under Article VIII and Section 8.6 of the Settlement Agreement; and (b) identification of counsel selected by the Indemnifying Party to defend the Third-Party Claim, which counsel must be reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party. The Indemnified Party shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay its acceptance of proposed counsel. If the Indemnifying Party does not deliver a timely Defense Notice within the twenty (20) Business Day period, the Indemnified Party shall have the right to defend the Third-Party Claim at the Indemnifying Party's reasonable expense, subject to the caps, baskets, deductibles, and other limitations of the applicable indemnification provision under Article VIII.

### 3.2 Conduct of Defense by Indemnifying Party

If the Indemnifying Party timely delivers a Defense Notice and assumes the defense of a Third-Party Claim, the following provisions shall apply:

(a) The Indemnifying Party shall have sole control of the defense of the Third-Party Claim and all related proceedings, including the selection and direction of defense counsel, the formulation and execution of litigation strategy, the conduct of discovery, and the management of all pre-trial, trial, and appellate proceedings.

(b) The Indemnifying Party shall keep the Indemnified Party reasonably informed of the status of the defense, including providing to the Indemnified Party copies of all material pleadings, correspondence, and court orders within ten (10) Business Days of receipt or filing thereof.

(c) The Indemnifying Party shall not consent to the entry of any judgment or enter into any settlement of the Third-Party Claim unless such judgment or settlement: (i) involves only the payment of money damages for which the Indemnifying Party is solely responsible; (ii) does not impose any injunctive relief, equitable remedy, or consent order on the Indemnified Party; (iii) does not contain any admission of liability, fault, or wrongdoing by or on behalf of the Indemnified Party; and (iv) includes a full and unconditional release of the Indemnified Party from all liability with respect to the Third-Party Claim. Any proposed settlement or judgment that includes non-monetary relief, including injunctive relief, equitable remedies, consent orders, or admissions of liability by the Indemnified Party, shall require the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

### 3.3 Indemnified Party's Right to Participate

Regardless of whether the Indemnifying Party assumes the defense of a Third-Party Claim, the Indemnified Party shall be entitled to participate in (but, if the Indemnifying Party has assumed the defense, not to control) the defense of such Third-Party Claim at the Indemnified Party's own cost and expense, using counsel of its own choosing. The Indemnified Party's separate counsel shall have the right to attend all proceedings, receive copies of all pleadings and material correspondence, and consult with the Indemnifying Party's counsel on material strategic decisions. The Indemnified Party's separate counsel shall not, however, have the right to direct or control the defense or to take any action inconsistent with the Indemnifying Party's defense strategy without the prior written consent of the Indemnifying Party.

### 3.4 Conduct of Defense by Indemnified Party

If the Indemnifying Party declines to assume the defense of a Third-Party Claim or fails to timely deliver a Defense Notice within the period specified in Section 3.1, the Indemnified Party may defend the Third-Party Claim at the Indemnifying Party's reasonable expense, subject to the following conditions:

(a) The Indemnified Party shall conduct the defense in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, using counsel reasonably competent in the subject matter of the Third-Party Claim.

(b) The Indemnified Party shall not consent to the entry of any judgment or enter into any settlement of the Third-Party Claim that would increase the Indemnifying Party's aggregate exposure beyond the applicable cap under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement without the prior written consent of the Indemnifying Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

(c) The Indemnified Party shall keep the Indemnifying Party reasonably informed of the status of the defense, including providing copies of all material pleadings, correspondence, and court orders within a commercially reasonable time following receipt or filing thereof.

(d) Reasonable defense costs and expenses incurred by the Indemnified Party in connection with such defense, including reasonable attorneys' fees, expert witness fees, and costs of document production and discovery, are recoverable as part of the indemnification claim under Article VIII, subject to the applicable cap, basket, deductible, and other limitations under the relevant Section of Article VIII.

## Section 4 --- Cooperation Obligations

### 4.1 General Cooperation

Each Indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation to the Indemnifying Party (and its counsel) in connection with the defense of any Third-Party Claim for which indemnification is sought under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, including without limitation:

(a) making available to the Indemnifying Party and its counsel all documents, records, files, correspondence, and data in the Indemnified Party's possession, custody, or control that are relevant to the Third-Party Claim;

(b) making available officers, directors, employees, agents, and other representatives of the Indemnified Party for interviews, depositions, trial testimony, and other proceedings as reasonably requested by the Indemnifying Party or its counsel;

(c) executing such powers of attorney, authorizations, or other documents as may be reasonably necessary to enable the Indemnifying Party to conduct the defense effectively; and

(d) otherwise cooperating in good faith with all reasonable requests of the Indemnifying Party relating to the defense, investigation, or resolution of the Third-Party Claim.

### 4.2 Costs of Cooperation

The reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by the Indemnified Party in fulfilling its cooperation obligations under Section 4.1, including travel expenses for witnesses, costs of document collection, review, and production, and similar direct costs, but expressly excluding fees and expenses of the Indemnified Party's separate counsel retained under Section 3.3, shall be borne by the Indemnifying Party. The Indemnified Party shall submit itemized invoices for such cooperation costs on a monthly basis, and the Indemnifying Party shall reimburse such costs within thirty (30) days of receipt of each such invoice.

### 4.3 Preservation of Privileges

Nothing in this Exhibit D shall require any Party to waive the attorney-client privilege, attorney work product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or immunity recognized under the laws of the State of Washington or any other applicable jurisdiction. If the cooperation obligations set forth in Section 4.1 require or may require the production of materials that are or may be protected by the attorney-client privilege, work product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to enter into a joint defense agreement or common interest agreement, as appropriate, to preserve all applicable privileges. The production of documents or information pursuant to any such agreement shall not constitute a waiver of any privilege with respect to such documents or information.

## Section 5 --- Insurance Coordination Procedures

This Section 5 sets forth the procedures for coordinating indemnification obligations under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement with available insurance recoveries, as contemplated by Section 8.7 of the Settlement Agreement.

(a) **Obligation to Pursue Insurance.** Prior to submitting a claim for indemnification under the procedures set forth in Section 6 of this Exhibit D, the Indemnified Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to submit the Third-Party Claim to any applicable insurance carriers and to pursue available insurance recoveries in respect of such Third-Party Claim. By way of illustration and without limitation, Cascadia maintains a Pollution Legal Liability insurance policy (Policy No. PLL-2023-08841) issued by Hollcroft Point Surety Group, with a fifteen million dollar (\$15,000,000) aggregate limit, a five hundred thousand dollar (\$500,000) per-occurrence self-insured retention, and a policy period running from January 1, 2023 through January 1, 2028. Each Indemnified Party shall be responsible for identifying and submitting claims to all applicable insurance policies in a timely manner consistent with the terms and conditions of such policies.

(b) **Reporting of Insurance Developments.** The Indemnified Party shall notify the Indemnifying Party of the status of any pending insurance claim related to a Third-Party Claim within fifteen (15) Business Days of any material development regarding such insurance claim, including without limitation any coverage determination, reservation of rights letter, denial of coverage, settlement offer from the insurer, or payment of insurance proceeds.

(c) **Dollar-for-Dollar Offset.** Indemnification payments made or payable under Article VIII shall be reduced on a dollar-for-dollar basis by insurance proceeds actually received by the Indemnified Party in respect of the same Third-Party Claim and related Losses.

(d) **No Requirement to Litigate Against Insurer.** The Indemnified Party shall not be required to initiate litigation or arbitration against its insurance carrier as a condition to seeking or receiving indemnification under Article VIII. The Indemnified Party must, however, at a minimum: (i) file a timely proof of loss or claim with the applicable carrier; (ii) respond to all reasonable information requests and document demands from the insurer in a timely and complete manner; and (iii) exhaust any internal appeals processes offered by the insurer before the indemnification claim may be treated as ripe for payment under Section 6 of this Exhibit D.

(e) **Remittance of Subsequent Insurance Proceeds.** If insurance proceeds relating to a Third-Party Claim are received by the Indemnified Party after the Indemnifying Party has already made an indemnification payment in respect of the same Third-Party Claim, the Indemnified Party shall promptly, and in no event later than fifteen (15) Business Days following receipt of such insurance proceeds, remit to the Indemnifying Party an amount equal to the lesser of (i) the insurance proceeds so received and (ii) the aggregate indemnification payments previously made by the Indemnifying Party in respect of such Third-Party Claim.

## Section 6 --- Calculation and Payment of Indemnification Claims

### 6.1 Submission of Indemnification Claims

Following the final resolution of a Third-Party Claim, whether by entry of a final, non-appealable judgment, execution of a settlement agreement, order of dismissal, or other final disposition, the Indemnified Party shall submit to the Indemnifying Party a written indemnification claim that includes:

(a) a copy of the final judgment, settlement agreement, order of dismissal, or other document evidencing the final resolution of the Third-Party Claim;

(b) an itemized accounting of all Losses (as defined in Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement) incurred by the Indemnified Party in connection with the Third-Party Claim, supported by reasonable documentation, including invoices, receipts, and expense summaries;

(c) documentation of any insurance proceeds received or pending in connection with the Third-Party Claim, including copies of any relevant correspondence with insurance carriers;

(d) a calculation of the indemnification amount due from the Indemnifying Party, giving effect to the applicable cap, basket or deductible, insurance offset, and any other limitation under the relevant Section of Article VIII; and

(e) a certification, signed by an authorized officer or representative of the Indemnified Party, that the claim does not fall within the Excluded Claims set forth in Section 8.6 of the Settlement Agreement.

### 6.2 Payment Terms

The Indemnifying Party shall pay all undisputed indemnification amounts within forty-five (45) days of its receipt of a complete indemnification claim submitted in accordance with Section 6.1. Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated in writing by the Indemnified Party. Interest shall accrue on any undisputed indemnification amount that remains unpaid after the expiration of such forty-five (45) day period at the rate of the lesser of (a) one percent (1%) per month, compounded monthly, or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, calculated from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is made in full.

### 6.3 Disputed Claims

If the Indemnifying Party disputes all or any portion of an indemnification claim submitted under Section 6.1, it shall deliver a written notice of such dispute (a "Dispute Notice") to the Indemnified Party within thirty (30) days of the Indemnifying Party's receipt of the indemnification claim. The Dispute Notice must identify with reasonable specificity the items or amounts in dispute and the factual and legal basis for each such dispute. The Indemnifying Party shall pay any undisputed portion of the indemnification claim in accordance with the payment terms set forth in Section 6.2 while the disputed portion is being resolved. All disputed amounts shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article IX of the Settlement Agreement, and any award or determination resulting from such procedures shall be final and binding on the Parties.

## Section 7 --- Multiple Indemnifying Parties

In the event that a Third-Party Claim may trigger indemnification obligations of more than one Indemnifying Party under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement (for example, a government cost recovery action under Section 8.4 that implicates the proportional cross-indemnification obligations of all three Settling Parties), the following procedures shall apply:

(a) The Indemnified Party shall deliver a Claim Notice to each Indemnifying Party that may bear an indemnification obligation with respect to such Third-Party Claim, in accordance with Section 2 of this Exhibit D.

(b) The Indemnifying Parties shall coordinate among themselves to determine which Party or Parties will assume the defense of the Third-Party Claim, and shall notify the Indemnified Party of such determination within the twenty (20) Business Day period specified in Section 3.1.

(c) If the Indemnifying Parties are unable to agree on the assumption of defense within the twenty (20) Business Day period, the Indemnified Party may designate one Indemnifying Party to lead the defense or, alternatively, may assume the defense itself in accordance with Section 3.4, with costs allocated among the Indemnifying Parties as set forth below.

(d) Each Indemnifying Party's contribution to any indemnification payment, settlement amount, or defense costs shall be determined in accordance with the proportional allocations set forth in the applicable Section of Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, including without limitation the cost share percentages of sixty-two percent (62%) for Cascadia, twenty-eight percent (28%) for Northshore, and ten percent (10%) for Puget Metalworks with respect to Section 8.4 government cost recovery claims, or the sixty percent (60%) / forty percent (40%) allocation applicable to Section 8.5 natural resource damage claims.

## Section 8 --- Subrogation

Upon making any indemnification payment under Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement and the procedures set forth in this Exhibit D, the Indemnifying Party shall be subrogated, to the extent of such payment, to all rights, claims, and remedies of the Indemnified Party against any third party (other than another Settling Party) with respect to the Third-Party Claim that gave rise to the indemnification obligation. The Indemnified Party shall execute such documents and take such other actions as are reasonably necessary to enable the Indemnifying Party to exercise and perfect such subrogation rights, at the Indemnifying Party's sole cost and expense. The Indemnified Party shall not take any action that would materially impair or diminish the Indemnifying Party's subrogation rights without the prior written consent of the Indemnifying Party.

## Section 9 --- Exclusive Remedy

The indemnification procedures set forth in this Exhibit D, together with the substantive indemnification provisions of Article VIII of the Settlement Agreement, shall constitute the exclusive remedy of the Settling Parties with respect to Third-Party Claims covered by Article VIII, except to the extent that any Party has remedies arising under the consent decree entered in this action or under Agreed Order No. DE-2021-04892, or as may be otherwise provided under Section 8.4 (Government Cost Recovery) of the Settlement Agreement or by applicable law. Nothing in this Exhibit D shall limit or restrict the rights of the Washington State Department of Ecology ("Ecology") or any other governmental authority under the consent decree, the Model Toxics Control Act (RCW 70A.305), or any other applicable statute, regulation, or order.
